rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window for all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs. A moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a useful baseline while limiting the risk of missing strongly retained compounds.

All pairs have excess resolution, so halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty. Keeping the solvent window and temperature unchanged will reveal which critical pairs are sensitive to gradient steepness.

The faster gradient removes the time penalty but compresses a central cluster. Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity separates that cluster without sacrificing speed.

Use an intermediate temperature to avoid the near-coelution seen at 60 C, with a slightly shallower gradient to improve the central separations. The last peak should remain near the zero-time-penalty window.

Increase temperature by one grid step to separate the remaining close central pair while retaining the improved resolution from the 12-minute gradient. This tests a selectivity compromise between 50 C and the different coelution observed at 60 C.

Injection 5 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the best method. Test a slightly shallower gradient for additional separation margin while aiming to keep the last peak within the zero-time-penalty window.

The maximum CRF is already secured. Shift injection 6’s solvent window upward while preserving its slope to test whether retention can be shortened without losing baseline separation; the first peak is still sufficiently retained to justify this small increase in starting organic fraction.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 7 to improve its sole under-resolved pair while preserving the favorable central separation. This may recover the maximum CRF with a shorter retention time than injection 6.

One further decrease in gradient slope should raise the limiting resolution above 1.5 while retaining separation of the other central pair. The last peak is projected near 8 minutes, so this tests a potentially better separation margin at the maximum CRF.

The maximum score is already secured; this tests another balance of starting strength and gradient slope. A higher starting organic fraction should shorten retention, while the shallower slope may preserve baseline separation with the last peak still near 8 minutes.

The maximum CRF is already secured at 55 C. Test the unexplored low-temperature selectivity regime with the fast gradient to see whether it resolves the central cluster while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity with a gradient slope between injections 5 and 6. The narrower solvent window should still encompass all peaks and preserve maximum CRF while reducing the programmed gradient duration.

Use a slope between injections 8 and 9 to seek baseline separation with slightly shorter retention than injection 9. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution composition, limiting the risk of hold-phase elution.

Maximum CRF is already secured, so test a substantially faster alternative. The higher starting organic fraction and steeper gradient may move the close pair seen at 60 C through its selectivity crossover and restore separation in a different elution order.

Increase starting organic by one step to test whether the remaining close pair at 60 C separates further after its apparent order reversal. Injection 14 has useful resolution margins elsewhere, making this a plausible route to a faster maximum-score method.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the remaining selectivity bottleneck, using a longer gradient to protect neighboring separations. Monitor the first pair closely because its retention and resolution may become limiting; the established maximum-score methods remain the benchmarks.

Return to the low starting organic fraction to protect early retention and test the unexplored 45 C selectivity at the successful gradient duration. This checks for an alternative separation regime between the central-cluster patterns at 40 and 50 C, while retaining the established maximum-score method.

Refine around the maximum-score methods at 55 C with a slope slightly shallower than injection 9. This should strengthen the earlier critical separation while testing whether the later pair and last-peak time retain sufficient margin for CRF 1.000.

Preserve injection 5’s successful gradient slope and temperature while ending the programmed gradient two minutes earlier. All peaks should elute before the shortened gradient ends, so this should retain the maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Trim the final organic fraction further while preserving the gradient slope of the maximum-score method. The estimated last-peak elution fraction is about 0.57, so all ten peaks should still elute within the gradient with unchanged separation and CRF.

Trim injection 9’s gradient endpoint while preserving its slope and its stronger minimum resolution of 1.58. The last peak’s estimated elution fraction is about 0.56, below the proposed endpoint, so this should retain the maximum CRF with all peaks inside the gradient.

Test one step steeper than injection 19 to locate the fast edge of the maximum-score region. This should shorten retention, although the central pairs’ small resolution margins may make this the limiting slope; injection 5 remains the established optimum.

Refine near injection 18 with a slightly shallower gradient and a lower endpoint that still exceeds the last peak’s elution composition. This should preserve baseline separation while testing the slow edge of the zero-time-penalty region; the maximum CRF is already secured.

Test one small slope decrease from injection 23 to locate the time-penalty boundary while maintaining baseline separation. The maximum CRF is already secured, and injection 9 remains the benchmark for separation margin among the maximum-score methods.

Use the final injection for one small slope refinement beyond injection 24, testing whether its limiting pair remains baseline-resolved before a time penalty appears. Injection 5 already achieves the theoretical maximum CRF and remains the campaign’s best method.
